s1.syndrome_frame: Post-liver transplantation fulminant liver failure with hemodynamic shock and cholestasis
salient_findings: Intra-abdominal bleeding from a choledochal artery branch
key_facts: 52-year-old man with HCV-associated end-stage cirrhosis
Underwent liver transplantation
Required relaparotomy due to intra-abdominal bleeding
Initial liver function improved
Cholestasis observed on day 4
Persistent abdominal pain reported on day 6
Fulminant liver failure and hemodynamic shock developed by day 7
Single fever peak of 38.4°C on day 8
Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, GGT, ALP) on day 6
Total bilirubin level of 119 μmol/L on day 6
Positive blood culture on day 7
Positive liver graft, colon, and small bowel biopsy samples on day 9

shortlist.label: Sepsis-induced Cholestasis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive blood culture and clinical presentation of fulminant liver failure with hemodynamic shock

shortlist.label: Primary Graft Dysfunction
shortlist.why_kept: Initial liver function improvement followed by rapid deterioration post-transplant

shortlist.label: Graft Rejection
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of fulminant liver failure and hemodynamic shock post-transplant

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus Hepatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever peak and liver dysfunction post-transplant, a common time frame for CMV reactivation

shortlist.label: Hepatitis C Virus Recurrence
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of HCV-associated end-stage cirrhosis and liver transplantation

raw.rationale: The patient's initial liver function improvement followed by rapid deterioration with fulminant liver failure, hemodynamic shock, and diffuse liver necrosis without vascular thrombosis or biliary leakage suggests primary graft dysfunction, which is a common cause of early graft failure after liver transplantation.

rejected.label: Sepsis-induced Cholestasis
rejected.why: While the patient had a positive blood culture, the primary issue seems to be graft dysfunction rather than sepsis causing cholestasis.

rejected.label: Graft Rejection
rejected.why: Graft rejection typically occurs later after transplantation and is not usually associated with such rapid deterioration and diffuse liver necrosis.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus Hepatitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of CMV infection or symptoms suggestive of CMV hepatitis in the provided case details.

rejected.label: Hepatitis C Virus Recurrence
rejected.why: Recurrence of HCV would not typically cause such rapid and severe liver dysfunction immediately after transplantation.
